purpose: Ziprasidone is used to treat schizophrenia and bipolar disorder. It helps reduce symptoms like hallucinations, delusions, and mood swings. It can also be used for short-term treatment of agitation in people with schizophrenia.
how_it_works: Your brain uses chemical messengers called dopamine and serotonin to communicate. When these chemicals are out of balance, it can cause symptoms like hallucinations or extreme mood changes. Ziprasidone helps balance these chemicals so your brain works more smoothly.
common_side_effects: You may feel drowsy, dizzy, or lightheaded, especially when standing up quickly. Some people experience nausea, upset stomach, or a runny nose. You might also notice restlessness or mild muscle stiffness when first starting the medication.
warnings: This medication can affect your heart rhythm, so tell your doctor if you have any heart problems or take other medications that affect the heart. It may increase your blood sugar and cholesterol levels, so regular checkups are important. Elderly patients with dementia-related conditions should use this medication with caution as it carries serious risks in that group. Avoid stopping suddenly without talking to your doctor first.
typical_dosing: For schizophrenia, the usual starting dose is 20 mg taken twice a day with food. Your doctor may gradually increase this up to 80 mg twice a day depending on how you respond. Always take this medication with a meal because food helps your body absorb it properly.
